title: Worker open_session non-authority ceiling for F1.select-1
purpose: Decide whether the non-authority part of worker open_session can make F1 (<10ms scenario) reach the frozen 20% gate. This is an upper-bound probe, not an optimization, not a capacity or SLA proof.

granted: durability commit timing, ordering and barrier placement

reference_arithmetic.expected_non_authority_share: 116.4 / 714 = 16.3%, below the 20% gate; the probe verifies the split and looks for unaccounted nonlinear cost

environment.host: macOS arm64, Docker 29.4.0 (OrbStack), linux/arm64 containers, host network, no TLS
environment.observers: PERI_DURABILITY_OBSERVER, PERI_SQL_OPEN_OBSERVER and PERI_COMPLETION_JOURNAL unset in all Stage B A/B legs
environment.volumes: fresh named volume per leg with prefix peri-r74-probe-; no existing peri-* volume is reused or deleted
environment.containers: one container per leg: same image, same launcher, same flags, fresh volume. The launcher fails closed on a dirty run directory, so a dirty volume is never reused. This is the R73 convention and the only supported way to get a clean proof per leg.
environment.interface: no TLS; no secret leaves the connection.json copy; any Authorization output is redacted as Bearer <REDACTED>

stage_a.goal: Cheap zero-code screen on the release image as-is

metric.primary: open_action_mean_ns = action_latency_ns_total['open'] / actions_total['open'] from the settled /v1/metrics snapshot
metric.quantile_limitation: the platform exposes only a per-action sum and count, no quantiles. For a right-skewed latency this mean is an upper bound on p50, so a below-threshold mean is a conservative stop condition; an above-threshold mean does not prove p50 is above the threshold, which is exactly why the rule then enters Stage B.
controls: session_by_id (record absence if the key does not exist)
metric.client_control: median of the 125 timed F1 durations in the harness raw.jsonl (client-side p50)

decision.fallback: if actions_total has no 'open' key, record the available keys, estimate from the client F1 p50 and the open-path relation, and enter Stage B when still undecidable

arms.A: worker built from main@518c40d (the v1.2.8 source) with the same rust toolchain and flags as B; platform is the v1.2.8 image's own /usr/local/bin/peri-platform for both arms
arms.B: probe worker from probe/r74-session-connect-ceiling with PERI_R74_CONNECT_POOL=1; PERI_R74_SEGMENTS unset
arms.why_local_A: building A and B with the same toolchain isolates the probe patch; Stage A separately measures the release image's own binaries, so any image-vs-local gap remains visible in the evidence

stage_b.pool_arm_definition: a background refiller keeps 1-2 pre-connected and pre-configured native turso connections per RemoteDatabase; Database::session() pops one when available and otherwise falls back to an inline connect; each connection serves exactly one session and is then dropped without reset

segmentation.kind: diagnostic only, never used for the A/B judgment
segmentation.run: B worker with PERI_R74_SEGMENTS=1 and PERI_R74_CONNECT_POOL=0, one fresh stack, at least 1000 F1 requests
segmentation.output: worker stderr summary lines 'R74WORKER opens=<n> ...' emitted every 500 completed opens
segmentation.assertion: each segment's sample count equals the completed open count of the same process; a mismatch invalidates only the segmentation data

build.record: worker SHA256 for both arms, platform SHA256, launcher SHA256

block_protocol.block: 100 consecutive F1.select-1 json-pipeline requests; block value = wall clock nanoseconds / 100
block_protocol.round_side_statistic: median of the two leg statistics of that side in that round
block_protocol.secondary_diagnostic: median of all individual request durations per leg (client p50), per-block p50 and per-block mean, reported but not judged
block_protocol.driver: a probe-side Python driver reusing scripts/perf-reliability/issue28/hrana.py; 100 requests are issued back-to-back on one keep-alive connection

decision.invalid_leg: any outcome_unknown, HTTP 502, HTTP 503, audit_unavailable, or broken audit chain invalidates that leg; fix the environment and re-run; the invalid leg and the re-run are both reported

invariants: container and worker binaries SHA256 recorded per leg
observers off in every A/B leg
settle check: session_seats=0, active_permits=0, unknown_held_permits=0, worker sessions=0, pending close=0
audit chain continuous from head to tail
deviation_policy: After this freeze, do not change criteria, sample sizes, quotas, ports or statistics. Environment events are recorded and labelled 'not attributed to this round'. Any invalidated leg is re-run, never silently accepted.

must_report: criteria.json SHA256 and UTC freeze time, and that no measurement leg existed at freeze
Stage A: image digest, container binary SHA256, per-action totals and open mean, client F1 p50, decision
Stage B: probe branch and commit SHA, worker SHA256, segment p50/p95 with counts, each round/leg block-average raw numbers, both round directions, F1/L1/X1 results, regression observations
final verdict: continue implementing or close the direction, with the raw evidence path
